name: atr_breakout_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when a 5-second candle's range exceeds 1.5× the recent 2-minute average true range, it signals that a large directional market order has swept multiple price levels within a single 5-second window — characteristic of institutional algo execution (TWAP/VWAP programs) that have initiated a directional leg. These programs typically fill only 30-60% of their intended size per burst, leaving continuation pressure that persists for the next 30-90 seconds. We enter at the close of the expansion candle in the direction of the bar (bullish close → CE, bearish close → PE), capturing the continuation leg before the program order is complete.

indicators.name: atr_24
indicators.purpose: 24 bars = 2 minutes of rolling average true range. NOT 12x the original 14-bar period (which would give 168 bars = 14 minutes). We compress because our hold is 15-60 seconds — we want to measure the local micro-volatility regime at the same timescale as our trade, not the session-scale regime. A 14-minute ATR would be too slow to reflect intraday volatility shifts; a 2-minute ATR captures the current burst regime.

indicators.name: bar_range
indicators.purpose: Current 5-second candle range compared against ATR to detect volatility expansion.

indicators.name: vol_mean_60
indicators.purpose: 60-bar (5-minute) rolling volume average for the NIFTY index. Adapted from the original 20-bar average on 1-minute stocks. At 5s frequency, index volume is noisy tick-by-tick; 5 minutes gives stable baseline to detect genuine activity surges vs. noise.

buy_ce.confirmation: All three on same bar; enter at bar close

buy_pe.confirmation: All three on same bar; enter at bar close

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option points corresponds to ~6 NIFTY spot points at ATM delta ~0.5. A genuine ATR breakout should not retrace more than 6 spot points within 30 seconds — if it does, the 'large program order continuation' thesis is wrong and the expansion was noise. At 5-second hold we need tight stops.
exit.target_rationale: 5 option points (~10 NIFTY spot points). A confirmed ATR expansion on NIFTY typically sees 10-20 spot point continuation in the burst direction (per observed 1-min burst behavior). 5 pts captures ~50% of the lower end of that range with 1:1.67 R:R, leaving room for the time stop to handle partial moves.

filters.vix_filter: none — VIX not used; ATR directly captures realized volatility regime
filters.time_filter: 09:20-15:25 IST; skip first 5 minutes of session (09:15-09:20) to avoid pre-open noise
filters.trend_filter: candle direction (close vs open) provides implicit trend/direction filter

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — structural. ATR breakout signals are widely known but the 5s granularity capturing institutional program continuation is less crowded than daily/weekly ATR strategies.

adaptation_notes: Original used ATR(14) on 1-minute bars with range > 1.5× ATR on NIFTY200 stocks. Three key adaptations: (1) Lookback compressed from 14×1min to 24×5s (2 minutes) — we trade at 5s so we need local micro-volatility, not session regime. (2) Direction added explicitly: original implied bullish/bearish by candle direction but didn't state it; we make it explicit with close vs open as the buy_ce/buy_pe switch. (3) Universe changed from equity stocks to NIFTY index — on the index, single-stock noise is averaged away and what remains is purer institutional order flow, making ATR expansions more signal-rich.
weaknesses: False signals during news spikes (RBI, FOMC) where range expands but no continuation follows
At 5-second resolution, individual large trades can create transient range expansion without institutional follow-through
Volume filter on index may fire too loosely during high-vol sessions
Range expansion candles on NIFTY can sometimes be gaps between bids/offers at session boundaries rather than genuine program flow
